tasks.short: She prepares and implements remedial programs for students who need extra help.

steps.what: Name the students whose gaps need a remedial program
Draft remedial activities for the students she named

loop.input: The pupil gap note and the goal code she wrote in that note
loop.output: Remedial activities that cite only that gap
loop.check: Each activity maps to a goal she named or a sentence in her note, and no diagnostic label or support-need sentence appears that is not already in her note
loop.stop: One pass, or she marks the line unknown and writes the activity herself
loop.why_not_simpler: The notes are free text, so a fixed form cannot tell a real gap from a line she did not write

steps.what: Accept or rewrite that remedial program before teaching
Implement the remedial programs beside those students

tasks.design: She writes the pupil and the skill gap in {DOCS}, and a bounded draft proposes remedial activities that cite only that gap. She accepts or rewrites the outline, then teaches it beside the students. The outline is not sent out and is not stored as a formal plan.
tasks.previous_blocker: The gap is in her own words, and a fixed form would invent a diagnosis or skip the teaching.
tasks.enabler_now: A short loop can draft only from the goal and the note she already wrote, and stop when a line is not in that note.
tasks.still_hard: She still has to teach the extra help. The school must confirm whether the note holds health data and whether national school rules treat it as a formal plan. A model must not infer emotion or set the education level.
tasks.human_edge: She decides which students need extra help, whether an activity fits that child, and how to teach it in the room.

ambition.what: She sees a remedial activity for a pupil she named that week before the next extra-help slot, and she still chooses whether to teach it.

tasks.altitude: Less time goes to a blank page. She does not gain a right to leave a drafted activity untaught, or to treat a draft line as agreed with the parent.

reach.task: Adapt extra help when a gap is beyond this class
reach.learn: Which pupil and skill gap she named, and which activity she accepted, so they do not start from a blank note

evidence.claim: A draft can be limited to goals and sentences she already wrote, and rejected when it adds a label that is not in the note.
A model that sets the education level or evaluates learning outcomes that count is high-risk from 2 December 2027, so this draft does not set a level.
Inferring pupils' emotions is banned, so the draft does not read mood.
Under the WMS, staff consent to tools that can monitor staff, and parents and pupils follow the pupil-data rules.
A formal development plan is set within six weeks of enrolment after consulting parents and is evaluated yearly, so this remedial outline is not that plan.

assumptions: She produces the pupil, the skill gap in her own words, and the goal code in s1 before any draft runs. If the note is missing, she writes the activities herself and the loop does not run.
She keeps the goal codes and the acceptable activity kinds current. That upkeep is her time, in the incremental hours, not existing runtime.
The outline is not a formal development plan and is not sent to a parent. The school must confirm whether the note holds health data.
National rules on staff consent and on parent and pupil consultation apply before the tool reads pupil notes.
unknowns: Whether this school's remedial notes hold support needs that count as health data.
Whether those notes already live in the document store.
Whether parents must be consulted before a remedial activity is taught, under this school's own rules.
research_questions: What share of this hour is the blank outline, and what share is the teaching beside the pupil?

already_counted.description: She reads each drafted activity against the gap she wrote, inside the check before she teaches.

incremental.description: She keeps the goal codes and the acceptable activity kinds current so the draft cannot invent a label.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central net is 4 after 2 hours to keep the goal codes and activity kinds current. Low 1 when notes are too thin and she rewrites most outlines. High 3 when the notes are clear. She still teaches the extra help.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: She assigns class work and homework and grades what comes back.

steps.what: Choose which class work and homework to assign today
Tell the class the homework and the class work
Collect class work and homework at the end of the lesson
Retick closed items on class work the method already scored
Grade the open homework and the class work still on paper
Type the open class grade into pupil administration

tasks.design: Where the {LMS} already holds a correct or incorrect flag from the practice method, she stops reticking that item. She still chooses the work, tells the class, collects it, grades every open answer and every paper item, and types those marks into pupil administration in {OTHER}. A flag is not the mark.
tasks.previous_blocker: Closed items and open answers sat on the same paper, so the second tick looked like part of the marking.
tasks.enabler_now: The learning system already writes the closed flag when the pupil answers. Skipping a second tick needs no new map.
tasks.still_hard: Open answers and paper work still need her eye. A mark that counts is hers to set. A flag must not become that mark.
tasks.human_edge: She decides what to assign, how to read an open answer, and which mark to enter.

ambition.what: She decides which closed items to reteach from flags already in the learning system the same day, before she finishes the open homework.

tasks.altitude: The second tick of items the method already scored drops out. She does not gain a right to let a flag stand as the class grade.

reach.role: Teaching Assistants, Preschool, Elementary, Middle, and Secondary School, Except Special Education
reach.task: Help collect class work and homework
reach.learn: Which closed items already carry a method flag, so a second tick is not added while the work is collected

evidence.claim: ParnasSys stores pupil records and learning-goal tracking, and no model is named for marking.
Closed items can be marked by code, so ticking an item the method already scored is duplicate work. This design does not score open answers.
Evaluating learning outcomes is high-risk from 2 December 2027, so a method flag does not become a mark she did not accept.

assumptions: The practice method in the {LMS} writes pupil id, item id, and correct or incorrect when the pupil answers. That runtime is not her new effort. If the flag is absent, she marks the item in the grade step.
She does not keep a new answer list. Incremental hours are zero because no new map is hers to maintain.
Typing the open and paper marks into pupil administration still happens and is not removed. No parent message is sent.
Showing existing flags to her is pupil data, so national consent rules apply before the screen is used this way.
unknowns: Whether this school's learning system already flags closed items, or only some practice sets.
What share of returned class work is closed items that already have a flag.
research_questions: What share of marking time is the second tick of closed items the method already scored?

incremental.description: No new map, list or model. The flag is existing learning-system runtime, so ongoing upkeep is zero.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central net is 8, only the second tick, with no upkeep hours. Low 3 when few items already have a flag. High 6 when most closed items are flagged and she still grades every open and paper answer.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: She prepares, administers and grades tests and assignments of student progress.

steps.what: Prepare tests and assignments from the goals she chose
Administer the tests in the room and take in the scripts
Tick closed items on the tests in front of her
Add up the closed ticks on these tests
Grade the open test answers and set the progress mark
Type each progress mark from these tests into pupil administration

tasks.design: She prepares the test and the answer key in {DOCS}, gives the test in the room, and ticks every closed item herself. A configured sum in {SPREADSHEET} adds only those ticks. She grades the open answers, sets the progress mark, and types it into pupil administration in {OTHER}.
tasks.previous_blocker: The total sat on the same script as the open answers, so adding the ticks looked like the judgement.
tasks.enabler_now: A spreadsheet total of ticks she already wrote is ordinary configuration. It does not read the script.
tasks.still_hard: She must see every script. Open answers and the progress mark stay with her. A machine score of a test that counts is the failure this design refuses.
tasks.human_edge: She writes the key, sees each script, reads the open answers, and sets the mark.

ambition.what: She sees which closed items the class missed, from ticks she already made, before she finishes the open scripts.

tasks.altitude: Adding a column of her own ticks takes less time. She does not gain a right to skip a script or to let the total stand as the progress mark.

reach.role: Middle School Teachers, Except Special and Career/Technical Education
reach.task: See what this class was tested on before the pupils move up
reach.learn: Which goals the test covered and which closed items the class missed, stated as topics, not as a mark

evidence.claim: Adding ticks she already made is arithmetic. Reading an open answer is not, so only the column total is configured.
Tests that evaluate progress are high-risk from 2 December 2027, so she still sets the progress mark and types it herself.
Rescoring requests rose from 2,758 in 2024 to 64,489 in 2026, and computers first scored 58 percent of the 13,300-plus raised reading scores.

assumptions: She writes the answer key in the prepare step: item id and the correct option. She writes each closed tick in the tick step. The sum only adds those ticks.
The key is part of preparing the test, already inside that step. Incremental hours are zero because she keeps no separate item bank.
The closed total is not filed as the progress mark. She types the mark herself into pupil administration.
If the sheet is not set up, she adds the column herself and the machine step does not run.
unknowns: Whether this school adds closed ticks on paper or in a spreadsheet today.
What share of a test is closed items versus open answers.
research_questions: What share of test time is adding the closed ticks, versus reading the open answers?

already_counted.description: She reads the summed total while she sets the progress mark, inside that marking step.

incremental.description: No new item bank or model. The answer key is written inside the prepare step, so ongoing upkeep is zero.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central net is 6, only the adding-up, with no upkeep hours. Low 2 when tests are mostly open answers. High 5 when closed items are many and she still reads every script.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: She encourages students to persevere and to explore later learning.

steps.what: Notice students stalling on a challenging task in the room
Encourage those students to persevere with the challenging task
Name a learning opportunity those students can explore later

tasks.design: She notices a student stalling on a challenging task, encourages that student to persevere, and names a learning opportunity they can explore later. The words stay spoken in the room. Nothing is written down, and nothing reads emotion.
tasks.previous_blocker: The moment is in the room and depends on the child in front of her.
tasks.enabler_now: Nothing new makes this shorter. Leaving it as spoken work is the design.
tasks.still_hard: The encouragement has to be said by her, to that student, then. A tool must not infer emotion.
tasks.human_edge: She sees the stall, chooses the words, and names an opportunity that fits that child.
tasks.altitude: Her week on this task does not change. She does not gain a right to replace the spoken encouragement.

reach.task: Encourage a child who is stuck on a challenging task
reach.learn: That the words are spoken in the moment, and that a written line is not a stand-in for them

evidence.claim: The task is the spoken moment in the room. A tool does not shorten noticing, encouraging, or naming a next opportunity.
Inferring pupils' emotions is banned, so this task does not read mood from the room.

assumptions: No tool, map or list is introduced, so incremental hours are zero.
The words are spoken in the school day. They are not a versioned message.
Nothing infers emotion, and nothing is written down for this task.
unknowns: Whether some of this encouragement is already written into a note at this school. If it is, that note is outside this task.
research_questions: How often a stall is handled by a spoken line, and how often she changes the task instead?

incremental.description: No tool, map or list. Nothing new to maintain.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Nothing in the room is shortened. Low and high stay at zero because there is no mechanism and no upkeep.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: She still teaches the extra help, still assigns and marks, still gives the test in the room, and still says the encouragement. Less time goes to a blank remedial page, to reticking items a method already scored, and to adding a column of ticks. She does not gain a right to let a drafted activity stand untaught, or to let a method flag become the progress mark.
reach: Special Education Teachers, Elementary School: take the pupil and the skill gap she named, and see which remedial activity she already accepted.
Teaching Assistants, Preschool, Elementary, Middle, and Secondary School, Except Special Education: see which closed items already have a method flag so they do not retick them while collecting work.
Kindergarten Teachers, Except Special Education: hear that encouragement stays spoken in the moment, and that a written line is not a stand-in.
skills_to_grow: Write the pupil and the skill gap in her own words before a remedial draft runs.
Leave a method's existing closed score unticked and still read every open answer.
Keep the test key with the test she prepared and type the progress mark herself.
role.ambitious_version: On a morning after a test she sees which closed items the class missed before she finishes the open scripts, and a remedial activity is ready for a pupil she named that week. She still marks the open work, still enters the progress mark, and still says the encouragement aloud. She does not publish a program and she does not let a draft score leave as the mark.
